findings.summary: The hung-sink limits are described, but unconditional capture promises still contradict them in the class contract and release notes.
evidence: The StampingPipe docstring says close drains every byte already in the pipe and that the drain reads everything written before close, then says a hung sink stops draining and close may return while a write is still in flight.
The hung-sink test shows close can return with an incomplete capture; after the blocked write is released, later lines are dropped and counted.
The notes still promise every byte written before the pipe closes reaches the lane log, while listing sink failure or short writes as loss cases and mentioning a hung write only as a possible stall.
findings.action: Qualify the all-bytes guarantees to exclude a hung sink, and state that a hung write can leave bytes uncopied while the incomplete-capture error records the loss.

counterweight_triage.concern: R-004: family counts may be read as complete counts of all matching commands.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The notes say patterns can miss unusual spellings, and the docs label family starts as pattern matches. That accurately describes the reported counts; mirroring the omission caveat in the docs would be clearer but is not needed to prevent a misleading consumer claim.

next_move: Revise the unconditional capture statements for the hung-sink case before release lock-in. R-004 is adequately qualified for this review.
